units.title: Visual Language
units.essentialQuestion: How does the choice of shot type, angle, and camera movement shape what an audience feels?
units.description: Core focus: Shot types, camera angles, camera movement. Students build the foundational vocabulary of cinematography while immediately applying it in production.

lessons.title: Orientation, WeVideo & Premiere Setup, Syllabus
lessons.objective: Set up production tools, understand course expectations, and form project groups.

lessons.title: Shot Types (ELS, LS, MS, CU, ECU)
lessons.objective: Identify and demonstrate the five primary shot types and explain how each affects viewer emotion.
lessons.notes: Use final scene from The Good, the Bad & the Ugly. Three-way gunfight shows ELS→ECU progression perfectly.

lessons.title: Camera Angles (Eye Level, Low, High, Dutch Tilt)
lessons.objective: Explain how camera angle conveys power, vulnerability, and tension in film.
lessons.notes: Stranger Things (eye level), Avengers (low/high), Iron Man (Dutch tilt), Lion King (low angle).

lessons.title: Camera Movements (Static, Pan, Tilt, Dolly, Truck)
lessons.objective: Demonstrate five camera movements and explain the emotional effect of each.
lessons.notes: Moonrise Kingdom for truck, Inception for Dutch tilt. Connect to NxNW crop duster for dolly examples.

lessons.title: Review & Assessment – Shots/Angles/Movements Quiz
lessons.objective: Demonstrate mastery of shot types, angles, and camera movements through written and visual assessment.

lessons.title: Intro Video Project
lessons.objective: Create a short personal introduction video using WeVideo, practicing basic editing techniques.

lessons.title: Storytelling Through Shots Project (Group)
lessons.objective: Create a 1–2 minute short film using all five shot types to tell a story without dialogue.
lessons.notes: Shot list worksheet required. Reflection required. No dialogue required.

units.title: Production Fundamentals
units.essentialQuestion: How does every production decision — from script to final cut — serve the story's purpose?
units.description: Core focus: Scriptwriting, storyboarding, interviewing, editing, audio, lighting. Students apply visual language skills to structured production work while deepening their technical toolkit.

lessons.title: Editing Techniques – Cuts, Transitions, Pacing
lessons.objective: Explain how different editing techniques (cuts, transitions, pacing) shape viewer emotion and narrative flow.
lessons.notes: Needs slides created. Priority to create. Use NxNW crop duster scene as primary example.

lessons.title: B-Roll Competition
lessons.objective: Capture 10+ B-roll shots on campus demonstrating variety of angles and movements, then edit into a 1-minute video.
lessons.notes: No faces rule. Variety of angles/movements required. Class vote for best videos.

lessons.title: Scriptwriting & Teleprompter Writing
lessons.objective: Write broadcast-ready scripts using teleprompter formatting and conversational language.

lessons.title: Audio & Sound Design
lessons.objective: Apply proper microphone technique, audio level standards, and ambient sound principles to video production.

lessons.title: Storyboarding
lessons.objective: Create a professional storyboard using panel notation and shot descriptions for pre-production planning.

lessons.title: Rule of Thirds & Interview Framing
lessons.objective: Apply the rule of thirds to on-camera interview framing and explain why long-sided interviews are standard.

lessons.title: Interviewing Techniques
lessons.objective: Demonstrate open-ended questioning, active listening, and follow-up techniques in a video interview context.

lessons.title: Peer & Teacher Interview Projects
lessons.objective: Produce professional 2–3 minute interviews with both on-camera and long-sided framing, including B-roll.
lessons.notes: 6–7 questions required. 1 follow-up required. B-roll required. Transitions required.

lessons.title: Lighting Basics – Three-Point Lighting
lessons.objective: Explain and set up three-point lighting, comparing natural and artificial light for mood and shadow.

lessons.title: Genre Study – Introduction to Genre Conventions
lessons.objective: Identify genre conventions in film and explain how genre sets audience expectations.

units.title: Music, Narrative & Story
units.essentialQuestion: How does a composer's score become as powerful as the images on screen?
units.description: Core focus: Music in film, Hero's Journey structure, narrative planning. Students move from visual technique to full storytelling, culminating in two major projects before winter break.

lessons.title: Music in Film – Score vs. Source Music
lessons.objective: Distinguish between score and source music and analyze how Danny Elfman's score in Nightmare Before Christmas creates emotional tone.

lessons.title: Hero's Journey – 12 Stages
lessons.objective: Identify all 12 stages of the Hero's Journey using Star Wars, How to Train Your Dragon, and Bluey examples.

lessons.title: Music Driven Story Project
lessons.objective: Create a silent short film driven entirely by music and visuals, with no dialogue. Storyboard required.
lessons.notes: No dialogue. Instrumental music only. Storyboard required before filming.

lessons.title: Pre-Production Review & Storyboard Peer Feedback
lessons.objective: Apply peer review criteria to evaluate storyboards and provide structured, actionable feedback.

lessons.title: Hero's Journey Group Project
lessons.objective: Produce a group film OR slide analysis of an existing film demonstrating all 12 Hero's Journey stages.
lessons.notes: On-screen text labels required. All cinematography techniques required.

lessons.title: Traditions Video Project
lessons.objective: Create a 2–3 minute video about a family holiday tradition using green screen and all camera techniques.
lessons.notes: Green screen required. Storyboard + script approval required before filming.

lessons.title: End of Semester Review & Film Festival
lessons.objective: Screen final semester projects, reflect on growth, and celebrate class work at the Film Festival.

units.title: Cultural Awareness & Documentary
units.essentialQuestion: Whose stories aren't being told — and how do we use film to change that?
units.description: Core focus: Research-driven video production, documentary structure, voice-over narration, cultural storytelling. Students produce real content that airs on the school news broadcast.

lessons.title: Documentary Structure & Voice-Over Narration
lessons.objective: Explain documentary structure and demonstrate professional voice-over narration technique with visual support.

lessons.title: Visual Research – Archival Images & Citation
lessons.objective: Apply methods for finding, selecting, and properly citing archival images and footage in documentary work.

lessons.title: Lower-Thirds & On-Screen Graphics
lessons.objective: Design and implement lower-thirds, title cards, and on-screen text following broadcast best practices.

lessons.title: Black History Month Tribute Video
lessons.objective: Create a video tribute to a chosen historical figure. Top videos air on the Roaring Report news broadcast.
lessons.notes: Student choice from provided list. Top videos air on Roaring Report.

lessons.title: Women's History Month Video
lessons.objective: Produce a 1:30–2:00 min structured documentary about an influential woman. Top videos air on broadcast.
lessons.notes: Structured outline provided: background, impact, challenges, inspiration.

lessons.title: Epic Movie Trailer (Group Project)
lessons.objective: Create a shot-for-shot recreation of a real movie trailer using all original footage and green screen.
lessons.notes: All original footage required. Own props/costumes required. Studio title card required.

lessons.title: Tension & Conflict – How Editing Builds Pressure
lessons.objective: Analyze how pacing and editing techniques create tension in non-action scenes.

lessons.title: Story of Television Documentary (Group Project, Year A)
lessons.objective: Produce a 4–6 minute documentary about an assigned influential TV show including voice-over, lower-thirds, and original graphics.
lessons.notes: Lower-thirds required. 1 original graphic required. Voice-over required. 3 visual support types required.

units.title: Genre, Creative Voice & Capstone
units.essentialQuestion: What is your voice as a filmmaker — and what story can only you tell?
units.description: Core focus: Genre awareness, creative autonomy, capstone production. Students bring together everything from the year in their most ambitious work.

lessons.title: Short Film Structure – Studying Pixar Shorts
lessons.objective: Identify elements of a complete short film structure and analyze Pixar shorts as models.

lessons.title: Green Screen Advanced Techniques & Chroma Key
lessons.objective: Apply advanced chroma key troubleshooting and creative uses of green screen in production.

lessons.title: How-To Video Project
lessons.objective: Create a 1–3 minute tutorial video with voice-over narration and time-lapse on any topic of choice.

lessons.title: Commercial Swede (Group Project, Year A)
lessons.objective: Create a shot-for-shot low-budget recreation of a commercial or TV intro with own props and storyboard approval.
lessons.notes: 45 sec–1 min. Own props required. Storyboard approval required. Green screen required.

lessons.title: Film Festival Planning – Audience Awareness
lessons.objective: Develop a film festival planning strategy considering audience awareness and production timeline.

lessons.title: Film Festival Short Film (Group Project)
lessons.objective: Produce a 5–6 minute original short film with authentic creative vision for whole-school screening and vote.
lessons.notes: No instructions — authentic creative vision. Whole school screening. Student vote. 4 weeks production time.

lessons.title: End-of-Year Reflection Podcast
lessons.objective: Create a 7–10 minute edited podcast video reflecting on the full year of learning and production.
lessons.notes: Raw recording, no advance questions. B-roll from past projects required.

lessons.title: Film Festival Week – Whole School Screening
lessons.objective: Screen the Film Festival short films for the whole school, conduct student vote, and celebrate the year.
